chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from Muhammad ibn Sulayman al-Daylami, from his father, from a man who wrote to the Servant of God (peace be upon him):

He asks him: I deal with a people to whom I sell flour, making a profit of two dirhams per qafiz for a known period, and they ask me to give them dirhams in exchange for half a qafiz of flour. Is there a way for me so that I do not enter into the forbidden (riba/usury)?
So he (peace be upon him) wrote to him: 'Lend them the dirhams as a loan, and increase the price on them for half a qafiz by the amount you used to profit from them.'

key_terms.الْحَرَام: The forbidden (specifically riba in this context)
key_terms.الْقَفِيز: A traditional unit of volume for dry goods

ai.seo_question: How to sell goods on credit without riba according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the classical Shia juristic concept of 'hiyal' (legal stratagems) to avoid riba, specifically by decoupling the loan from the sale transaction. Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) advises separating the cash advance (qard) from the commodity sale (bay'), ensuring that the markup is attached to the goods rather than the money, thereby preserving the validity of the credit sale under Shariah principles.
